title: EGSE based on SCOS 2000: The EGSE & Mission Control System
short_title: EGSE based on SCOS 2000 (EMCS) User Manual
status_notes: Status 'Issue' (cover, PDF p. 1). Change log from issue 1.0 (8 June 2001, SCOS 2000 Release 2.1.1) through 3.5 (04 March 2004, final P5 updates) (PDF p. 2); covers the SCOS EGSE Release 2.3e P5 version delivered by ESTEC/TOS-EMG (PDF p. 7).
summary:
Issue 4.0 (9 March 2004) of the Software User Manual for the EGSE version of SCOS-2000 that ESTEC (TOS-EMG) prepared for the Herschel/Planck instrument developers, written by Serge Valera. The EGSE and Mission Control System (EMCS) follows the PROBA approach of one system for checkout and operations, using SCOS-2000 instead of SCOS-2. It consists of the SCOS-2000 kernel with its internal MIB, the SCOE system reached through an EGSE router and gateway, the Tcl/Tk-based Test and Operations Procedure Environment (TOPE), used while PLUTO (ECSS-E-70-32) tools were not available, and a Space System Model in which each addressable system element has a 16-bit identifier, with 0x0000-0x07FF reserved for on-board application processes (APIDs).

The manual covers installation of release 2.3e P5 on SuSE Linux 7.3, configuration and start-up. For MIB engineers the key part is section 4: the minimum EGSE data set (MIN_EGSE), whose files (tcp, pcdf, pcpc, ccf, cdf, cpc, dpc, pcf, plf, vdf) a mission adapts to its own packet headers; the 'Z' prefix of its names; SPIDs 1-100 reserved for generic packets; the mergeDATA and setSCOSdata tools; and the EGSE-specific MISCconfig variables (routing mode, binary command ZBINTC, time-stamping policy, mission epoch).

Section 6 is the TOPE language reference (tcsend with verification flags and time-tagging through PUS service 11,4; fetch, subscribe, waitfor, watchdog and logging). Section 7 defines the EGSE router message header and templates 1-7, an acknowledgement policy that extends PUS service 1 with ground-station, uplink and on-board acceptance reports (subtypes 9-14), and how SCOS files incoming messages by SPID, including unknown packets. Appendices cover conventions, known bugs and migration of procedures to the Herschel/Planck CCS.

key_points.text: The manual details the EGSE aspects of the EGSE version of SCOS 2000 prepared by the Agency and delivered to the Herschel/Planck instrument developers.

The EMCS follows the PROBA common EGSE and mission control system approach, with SCOS 2000 replacing SCOS2; it is made of the SCOS kernel with its internal MIB, the SCOE system, the test and operation procedure environment and the Space System Model.
System Element identifiers range over 0x0000-0xFFFF; 0x0000-0x07FF are reserved for on-board application processes and equal the APIDs, reflecting the 11-bit CCSDS APID field.

SE-ID allocation table: 0x0800 router (spacecraft identifier in MIB), EMCS clients 0x2000-0x2FFF, ground station processes 0x4000-0x4FFF, TC Front End 0x8800-0x880F, TM Front End VC0-VC7 0x8810-0x8817, EGSE gateway/router 0xF000-0xFFFF.
The Oracle-based SSM repository was not yet available, so users populate mission data through the SCOS 2000 ASCII (MIB) file interfaces, extended for EGSE command and control.
TOPE is a TCL/TK-based procedure environment provided because PLUTO (ECSS-E-70-32) compliant software was not yet available.
The MS-Windows EGSE Router (Delphi, DCOM/ActiveX, with a TCP/IP Gateway) and TM/TC Front Ends are not used in Herschel/Planck; SRON developed a Linux-based EGSE router for Herschel.
A mission adapts the MIN_EGSE data set (tcp, pcdf, pcpc, ccf, cdf, cpc, dpc, pcf, plf, vdf files) to its TM/TC packet headers; all MIN_EGSE parameter and command names start with 'Z'.
SPIDs 1 to 100 are reserved for the SCOS EGSE generic setup.

MISCconfig EGSE_MODE selects TC routing: 0 NCTRS only, 1 NCTRS and EGSE Router, 2 EGSE Router only (default 1); EGSE_BINCMD_NAME defaults to the binary command ZBINTC for commands not defined in the MIB.
EGSE_TM_FILING_TIME_TYPE time-stamps incoming TM by EMCS time (1), ground station/SCOE time (2) or uncorrelated OBT relative to TCO_MISSION_EPOCH (3), whose default is 1958-01-01T00:00:00.000000.

tcsend uses the MIB default acknowledgement flags (CCF_ACK and PCDF_VALUE where PCDF_TYPE='K') when no ack clause is given; executiontime builds an on-board schedule command (LOADTT, PUS service 11,4).
The EGSE router message header: DstID (2 octets), SrcID (2), Token (4), Time (8), Msg_Type (1), Spare (1), S/C id (2, 0x66 for PROBA), then application data.
Msg_Types: 1 SCOE command, 2 SCOE command verification report, 3 SCOE observation report, 4 sending TC packet request, 5 sending TC packet verification report, 6 TM packet report, 7 TM frame reports.
Besides the four PUS acknowledgements, the EMCS adds GS_Ack, UL_Ack and ONB_Ack, reported as service type 1 subtypes 9 to 14 (successful/failed GS, UL and on-board acceptance).
Incoming messages are filed in SCOS internal packets by SPID chosen from Msg_Type, APID, service type/subtype and the PI1/PI2 fields (per the Database Import ICD section 3.3.2.4.2).
TM packets with no matching pid.dat entry are filed under EGSE_WRAPPER_PKTID_6 and can be re-distributed into proper SPID archives with PDS_DISP after the MIB is updated.
Bit numbering convention: bit 0 is the first transmitted bit and the MSB of a binary value.
Known bug: time parameters before 1970 display wrongly; with a 1958 epoch a raw value of 0 shows as 2094.
On the H/P CCS each TOPE procedure runs as a separate process and must explicitly connect and attach to a SCOE before commanding it.

notes: Archive stamp SPIRE-ESA-DOC-002291; source file name EMCS-SUM4_0.doc. Printed page numbers equal PDF page indexes (page N of 72; the PDF has a trailing blank page). Inconsistencies as printed: the SE-ID table gives decimal 4099 for 0x1000 and 34816-36863 for 0x8000-0x8FFF (PDF p. 11); the MISCconfig defaults give 23 and 24 for EGSE_VER_TC_GS_PKTID and EGSE_VER_TC_REP_PKTID (PDF p. 24), whereas sections 7.7 and 7.8 cite SPIDs 10005 and 10006 (PDF pp. 54, 56); the EGSE_PIC_FILE_3/_6 variable names are repeated for the pid3.dat/pid.dat rows (PDF p. 25); section 5 refers to 'section 0' (broken cross-reference, PDF p. 26). Document IDs in the reference list are printed with stray spaces ('ECSS- E70-31', 'S2K-MCS- ICD-...'). Appendix D is an ESTEC-internal SuSE 7.3 installation recipe. [R5] is available in this library as icd-5-1-tos-gci; [A1] appears in cosmos-common-egse-document-overview as TOS-GCE/98.015/PSH.
